purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five individually registered Dublin City NIAH buildings in the Talbot Street and Gardiner Street Lower area

source_snapshot.queue_rule: Each selected registration number was checked as an exact entry in the workflow-generated Dublin missing-registration queue.

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.note: Official national CSV provides ITM coordinates and latitude/longitude. Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved separately as raw values because the page does not label their CRS.

candidate_records.name: XL Stop Shop/Airsoft Good Fellow
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010140 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced three-bay three-storey house built c.1880, now modified for two retail outlets with accommodation above. The NIAH records Flemish-bond red brick, a polychrome brick string course, three-centred-arch upper windows, timber sliding sashes and recent ground-floor shopfronts. The unusually proportioned façade contributes to the south-side Talbot Street terrace.

candidate_records.name: Clean City Laundrette
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010142 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey house built c.1820 with a ground-floor shopfront. The NIAH records Flemish-bond brickwork, a masonry cornice with foliate mouldings, gauged brick window openings, timber sliding sash windows and decorative cast-iron balconettes. Painted parapet lettering preserves the name of the former O'Neills Discount Jewellers business. The appraisal notes the railway viaduct disrupts the terrace to the west.

candidate_records.name: Durban House
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010149 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1825, with a two-storey hipped-roof rear return. The NIAH records Flemish-bond brown brick, granite plinth and coping, timber sliding sash windows, decorative cast-iron window boxes, a stucco Ionic doorcase, granite approach and iron railings. The appraisal places it in a long terrace extending from the Loop Line Bridge to Talbot Street and explains the planned Gardiner Street vista towards the Custom House.

candidate_records.name: Adelphi House
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010151 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1825. The NIAH records Flemish-bond brickwork, a granite plinth, timber windows, a stuccoed Ionic doorcase with laurel motifs, a shared granite platform and cast-iron railings. The appraisal identifies it as part of a largely intact Georgian terrace and notes that it is the only house in this stretch to have been painted. It retains its original door and doorcase.

candidate_records.name: PW Medical Centre
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010152 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1825. The NIAH record's structured In Use As field identifies a surgery/clinic, while its descriptive text says it is now in use as a guesthouse; this internal source discrepancy is preserved and not resolved by inference. The appraisal describes the house as part of the later c.1825 phase of the Georgian terrace from Nos. 63-70 and highlights the historic doorcase, cast-iron window boxes and fenestration.

duplicate_screen.method: Exact registration-number searches against open repository issues and pull requests.
duplicate_screen.result: No open issue or pull request matches returned for any of the five exact registration numbers at time of research.

spatial_and_identity_cautions: 50010140 and 50010142 are separately registered Talbot Street buildings. Their shared terrace context does not make them one object.
50010149, 50010151 and 50010152 are three separate registered houses at Nos. 69, 67 and 66 Gardiner Street Lower. Shared terrace fabric and party walls do not justify merging their identities.
50010152 has an internal discrepancy between the structured In Use As field and the narrative description. Preserve both source statements pending clarification; do not assert current use.
Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved as raw values because the page does not label their CRS. Do not interpret them as EPSG:2157 or overwrite official CSV coordinates.
NIAH descriptions of use, condition and alterations are survey-time source statements, not present-day field verification.
No physical access, ownership, public access or current condition has been verified.
explicitly_not_done: No visual inventory or source registry imports
No map pins or coordinate imports
